text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said he needed "a bit more time" to select candidate for the post of Chief Minister of Selangor state. Former Chief Minister Muhammad Muhammad Taib resigned earlier this month after being charged in an Australian court for bringing nearly $1 million in cash into the country.
-- Hungary has been invited to invest in Malaysian development projects by Prime Minister Mahathir. He extended the invitation to visiting Hungarian premier Gyula Horn on Monday.

-- An election court in the eastern state of Sarawak declared the ruling National Front coalition party's victory in a state seat election last year as null and void. The decision paves the way for a by-election in the constituency.
